newsitem.title: USA: ITT may get offer for Cuba telephone claims - paper.
newsitem.headline: ITT may get offer for Cuba telephone claims - paper.

text.p: ITT Corp has been in private contact with Italian telecommunications group STET International about a possible purchase of ITT's ownership claim to Cuba's telephone system, the Miami Herald said on Saturday.

Such a deal would unprecedented for a U.S. company and would allow STET to avoid possible U.S. sanctions against foreign companies exploiting U.S. properties seized after Cuba's revolution in 1959, the newspaper said.

Quoting unnamed U.S. government sources in Washington, the Herald described the ITT-STET contacts as preliminary and said that an agreement transferring ownership of the system valued at $131 million in 1970 was far from certain.
The Herald also quoted a spokesman for ITT, which is headquartered in New York, as saying there were no deal talks between STET and ITT.
ITT representatives in New York were not immediately available to comment to Reuters on the report. The company now has lodging, gambling, entertainment and information services operations.
In Rome, one was immediately available for comment at STET's offices in the Italian capital.

The newspaper said Clinton adminstration officials approve of the STET-ITT contacts, hoping a deal might eventually lead to cash payments for 5,910 other registered U.S. citizens and companies claiming ownership of properties in Cuba,
No U.S. company has sold property it held in pre-Castro Cuba since 1959.
STET is in a joint venture with the Cuban government in the island's telephone system. Cuba invited foreign companies during the early 1990s to invest in modernizing its telephone system.

STET told U.S. officials of the ITT contacts after the State Department warned it was violating the Helms-Burton law and the government would bar its executives from entering the United States, the Washington sources told the newspaper.
The administration is not now enforcing the Helms-Burton law against STET, the newspaper said.
